dedupe_keys.name: times ireland scenarios for the second carbon budget programme 2023 2024

description: The University College Cork Energy Policy and Modelling Group used TIMES-Ireland during 2023–2024 to support the Climate Change Advisory Council’s Second Carbon Budget Programme. The published application examines Irish energy-system pathways through 2050, focusing on proposed budgets for 2031–2040. It compares emissions constraints and demand assumptions across electricity, transport, buildings and industry. The official case page supplies the September 2024 report and related working-group material as public documents, available free; no explicit document reuse licence was identified. Reported scenarios connect tighter budgets with earlier emissions cuts, electrification and lower energy demand. Their technology and cost results support capacity planning and policy comparison. A limitation is that these are conditional least-cost pathways, not forecasts or evidence that measures were implemented. The report excludes several distributional and institutional effects from the model itself. Existing model-times-ireland-model records the software used. This later study is distinct from the first carbon-budget scenarios mentioned in that model record. The report was read remotely without saving its PDF.
name: TIMES-Ireland scenarios for the Second Carbon Budget Programme, 2023–2024
notes: G5 G5-0117. Software checked through metadata and documentation, without installation or execution. Geographic scope follows the documented application or software portability; it does not imply validation throughout that area.
outcomes: Conditional pathways identify earlier decarbonisation, demand reduction and electrification as important to tighter carbon budgets; results informed proposals rather than proving implementation.
provider: Climate Change Advisory Council / University College Cork Energy Policy and Modelling Group
